title: Douglas v. Deutsche Bank National Trust Co., No. 24-CV-1099, Published Order

reading.body:
The reports describe a court faulting lawyers for a Deutsche Bank subsidiary over an AI hallucination. The failure mode is a model asserting something false as fact, and it surfaced at the point of filing, where generated text entered a court record as though it were verified authority. The output was not a draft kept in-house, it was material put before a tribunal.

Catching it would have taken a check of the cited material against the record before the filing was submitted. A fabricated citation is detectable by looking for the source it claims to rest on, and that check is mechanical rather than a matter of legal judgment. Nothing in the deployment as described placed a human verification step between the model's output and the court.

What is not established is most of the case. The available summary of the published order is not a summary at all, it records only that the document could not be read, so the parties, the underlying dispute and any consequence for the lawyers are not established here. A court faulting lawyers, as reported, is a finding by that court, and these reports do not establish intent to mislead.
